title: Online Shopping Automation
notes: This presentation describes the current local project, playwrightProject1. It follows the 21-slide structure and native geometric layouts of the supplied CRM reference. No application brand or client identity is established by the code, so the title uses Online Shopping. The deck documents implemented coverage; it does not claim that the full suite passed. Sources: package.json, playwright.config.js, tests/, POM/.

Customer workflows, framework design and execution

title: Project Information
notes: The application under test is an online shopping website. The repository contains 11 spec files with one business test each, 24 files under POM, and one authentication setup test. Four product categories are used by the purchase workflow: Books, Fashion, Furniture and Electronics. The configured execution projects use Chromium. Client name and deployment ownership are not provided. Sources: package.json; tests/*.spec.js; POM/; playwright.config.js.

title: Framework Architecture
notes: Local CLI commands or CI invoke Playwright Test using playwright.config.js. Specs express scenarios and assertions; page objects provide locators and operations. JSON inputs and fixtures supply data and starting state. Reports and configured artifacts are produced during execution. POM is used with varying depth: some classes are locator holders, others include methods. Sources: playwright.config.js; tests/support/; POM/; testData/testData.json; Jenkinsfile.

title: Login & Logout
notes: TC-010 uses the shopping fixture to register and sign in a unique shopper. It verifies the welcome message and profile email, signs out, checks that the login link is visible and the logout link is absent, then opens and reloads my-account.php and verifies an empty profile email. This is a UI-level session check. Sources: tests/loginLogout.spec.js; POM/loginLogout.page.js; tests/support/shopping.fixture.js.

shapes.text: Validate account identity and signed-out behavior

Account email matches the created user.

Login link returns; logout link disappears.
Account email stays empty after reload.

title: Product Search & Cart
notes: Product search looks up a TV by the JSON-defined search term and verifies the product heading. Repeated Add to Cart opens a specific product and adds it three times. The test checks one row after each addition, and calls checkCart for quantities one and three. checkCart parses currency and checks row total = quantity * unit price + shipping, and grand total equals row total. The formula reflects this application and the current one-product cart. Sources: tests/searchProduct.spec.js; tests/repeatedAddToCart.spec.js; tests/support/cartVerification.js; POM/searchProduct.page.js.

Check price, shipping and totals.
Row total = quantity × unit price + shipping
For the tested single-product cart: grand total must equal the row total.

title: Wishlist Persistence
notes: TC-006 verifies a product persists in the wishlist after a logout/login cycle using the same generated account. It checks the product heading before saving, then one wishlist row and a visible product link after login. The test does not follow that link to recheck the details heading. The local let wishlist declaration shadows the outer variable, so the afterEach cleanup hook currently returns without cleanup. Sources: tests/wishlistPersistence.spec.js; POM/wishlistPersistence.page.js; tests/support/shopping.fixture.js.

shapes.text: A saved product should survive a new login
Persistence check: saved data remains available across the session boundary.

title: Wishlist to Cart
notes: TC-007 adds a saved wishlist product to the cart. It captures the displayed current price, excluding the old-price span, and compares it with the cart price. checkCart verifies one row, quantity one and totals. Reload must preserve the cart, and its link must open the correct product. Limitation: local let declarations shadow the outer wishlist/cart variables, so the afterEach cleanup hooks currently return without cleanup. The presentation does not claim cleanup succeeds. Sources: tests/wishlistToCart.spec.js; POM/wishlistToCart.page.js; tests/support/cartVerification.js.

shapes.text:

Open the product using its cart link.
Verify the expected product heading.

title: Product Reviews
notes: TC-008 creates a review summary containing a UUID, selects each configured rating and submits the form. After revisiting the same product URL it checks exactly one review with that summary, the reviewer name and review text. Submission-response checks and review-identifier attachments are commented out. The test suite implements no review-deletion operation, so submitted reviews remain. Sources: tests/productReview.spec.js; POM/productReview.page.js.

title: Password Change Validation
notes: This is an incorrect-current-password rejection scenario, not successful password-change coverage. The test signs in with the configured existing account, submits an invalid current password with a proposed new password, checks the configured error dialog, logs out and verifies that login with the original password still works. Sources: tests/changePassword.spec.js; POM/changePassword.page.js; testData/testData.json.

title: Checkout & Pending Payments
notes: The paymentPending scenario reuses shared saved authentication. It adds a book, proceeds to checkout without submitting payment, and opens the pending-payments view. The assertion checks the expected URL and a matching product heading. It can match an older entry and does not uniquely correlate the newly created order. Sources: tests/paymentPending.spec.js; POM/myAccount.page.js; playwright.config.js.

title: Purchase & Order Tracking
notes: The purchase test creates a unique account, signs in, adds one product from each of Books, Fashion, Furniture and Electronics, sets billing and shipping fields, reapplies billing as a workaround documented in the source, and submits the internet-banking option. It asserts the configured tracking-link count, captures each popup and logs out. It does not verify external payment settlement or assert each order status. The image is an existing repository artifact, screenshots/track-order-1.png; it shows Order Not Process Yet and is not evidence of a new run. Sources: tests/purchaseAndTrackOrder.spec.js; POM/trackproduct.page.js; screenshots/track-order-1.png.

title: Functional Dependencies
notes: Six specs import shopping.fixture: repeatedAddToCart, wishlistPersistence, wishlistToCart, productReview, updateProfile and loginLogout. Two specs use saved authentication: paymentPending and updateBillingAddress. Three remaining specs arrange their own starting state: searchProduct, purchaseAndTrackOrder and changePassword. The shared-state project depends on setup and a saved session file. The fixture performs session teardown but does not delete generated accounts. Sources: tests imports; tests/support/shopping.fixture.js; tests/auth.setup.js; playwright.config.js.

title: Execution & Reporting
notes: BASE_URL must be present in .env or the process environment and must use HTTP or HTTPS. The three active projects are setup, chromium-authenticated and chromium. workers is one. Retries are two when CI is truthy and zero locally. The global reporter is HTML and trace is on-first-retry. Six fixture specs override diagnostics to screenshot only-on-failure and trace retain-on-failure. No fresh suite run was performed for preparing this deck. An existing .last-run.json reports failed, but it is insufficient to compute a complete suite pass rate. Sources: playwright.config.js; tests/*.spec.js; test-results/.last-run.json.

title: CI & Delivery Workflow
notes: Jenkinsfile uses agent any but runs bat commands, so it requires a Windows-capable agent. BASE_URL is injected through the Project_BaseURL credential. The pipeline installs dependencies and browsers, runs tests, and publishes the HTML report when present. It does not explicitly set CI. GitHub Actions runs on Ubuntu for pushes/pull requests to main/master, uses npm ci and uploads the report with 30-day retention. It currently does not inject the required BASE_URL. The files establish intended CI behavior, not a successful run. Sources: Jenkinsfile; .github/workflows/playwright.yml; playwright.config.js.

title: Coverage & Next Improvements
notes: Coverage totals are based on 11 business tests in 11 spec files. Shopping and discovery: search, repeated cart, wishlist persistence, wishlist to cart, product reviews (5). Account management: login/logout, profile update, incorrect-password rejection, billing update (4). Checkout and orders: purchase/tracking and pending payments (2). The sample reference had an effort table, but this repository provides no approved estimates, so the deck uses verified inventory and future priorities. Improvement priorities include fixing shadowed cleanup references in wishlistToCart and wishlistPersistence, stronger exact-order assertions, account/review cleanup, environment configuration and enabling additional browsers. No pass rate or time saving is claimed.

shapes.text: Verify exact orders and stronger checkout outcomes.
